correctness.rationale: The statistic is a second factorial cumulant on the diagonal, not a variance. Write q=1−p and R=binom(n−a,b)/binom(n,b). Counting ordered disjoint pairs of connected components divides the product of the individual expected counts by the double counting of ab absent cross-edges and multiplies by the disjoint-set ratio R. Thus the normalized cumulant is R q^(−ab)−1 for a+b<=n and −1 when a+b>n; the means are positive for all in-scope sizes and 0<p<1. The unique feasible zero is π=1−R^(1/(ab)). The finite logarithmic average and positive Laplace representation are valid even at a+b=n. The strict log-convexity in size of (exp(tx)−1)/(x(exp(t)−1)) follows from 2 sinh(tx/2)>tx, giving the strict balancing comparisons, including the diagonal. Coordinate monotonicity is strict by adding a larger terminal row or column; the global extremes then give 1/n and 1−n^(−1/(n−1)), coinciding only at n=2. The ordering gives opposing ordinary covariances for (2,3) and (1,4) on an open interval for every n>=5. At n=5 and q=27/40, independent integer comparisons gave 40^6−10·27^6=221795110>0 and 5·27^4−40^4=97205>0 (replay: branches/review-exact-small-checks.js). The frozen verifier was inspected but not executed. The all-size conclusions were checked by proof, not inferred from finite enumeration.
